p.src: Our tale turns to the great city of Chang’an in Shaanxi, where emperors of successive dynasties had established their capitals. From the Zhou, Qin, and Han dynasties onward, its three regions had bloomed like brocade and eight rivers had flowed around the city; it was truly a celebrated land of scenic beauty. At that time Emperor Taizong of the Great Tang had ascended the throne and proclaimed the Zhenguan era. Thirteen years had passed since his accession; it was the year Jisi. Peace reigned under Heaven, tribute came from all eight quarters, and all within the four seas acknowledged his sovereignty.

p.src: One day, Taizong took his seat upon the throne and assembled all his civil and military officials. When the court salutations were over, Chancellor Wei Zheng stepped forward and memorialized: “All under Heaven is now at peace, and the eight quarters are tranquil. We should follow ancient custom, open the examination halls, summon worthy scholars, and promote men of talent to assist in enlightened government.” Taizong said, “Your memorial is well reasoned, worthy minister.” He therefore issued a proclamation seeking worthy men and circulated it throughout the realm: in every prefecture, subprefecture, and county, whether soldiers or commoners, all Confucian scholars who had read the classics, understood composition clearly, and mastered the three examination sessions were to proceed to Chang’an and sit the examination.

p.src: When this proclamation reached the region of Haizhou, a man surnamed Chen, given name E and courtesy name Guangrui, saw it and immediately returned home. He said to his mother, Madam Zhang, “The court has issued an imperial notice opening the southern provincial examination to select worthy talent. Your son wishes to go and sit for it. If I should gain even some modest official post, bring honor to my parents and fame to my name, win rank for my wife and privileges for my children, and shed glory upon our household, my ambition will be fulfilled. I have come especially to inform you before I leave.” Madam Zhang said, “My son, you are a scholar. ‘Study while young and put your learning into practice when grown’—this is precisely what you should do. Go and take the examination, but be careful on the road. Once you obtain office, return quickly.”

p.src: Guangrui ordered the household servant to pack his luggage, then bowed farewell to his mother and hurried on his journey. When he reached Chang’an, the examination halls had just opened, and Guangrui entered to sit the examination. When the examination was over, he was among those selected. Then, after answering three policy questions in the palace examination, he was personally awarded first place by the Tang emperor’s imperial brush and paraded on horseback through the streets for three days.

p.src: Unexpectedly, his procession passed the residence of Chancellor Yin Kaishan. The chancellor had a daughter named Wenjiao, also called Mantangjiao, who was still unwed. She had erected a lofty, festooned tower and was casting an embroidered ball to choose a husband. As it happened, Chen Guangrui was passing beneath the tower. The young lady saw at once that Guangrui was a man of exceptional bearing and learned that he was the newly appointed principal graduate. Delighted beyond measure, she cast down the embroidered ball, which struck Guangrui squarely on his black gauze cap. Suddenly there arose a soft harmony of reed pipes and flutes. More than a dozen maids hurried down from the tower, seized Guangrui’s horse by the bridle, and welcomed the principal graduate into the chancellor’s residence to be married. The chancellor and his wife immediately came into the hall, summoned the master of ceremonies to conduct the rites, and gave their daughter to Guangrui in marriage. After bowing to Heaven and Earth, the bride and groom bowed to each other, and then paid homage to the bride’s father and mother. The chancellor ordered a banquet prepared, and they drank merrily throughout the night. The two went hand in hand into the fragrant bridal chamber.

p.src: At the third watch of the fifth drum the next morning, Taizong took his imperial seat in the Golden Throne Hall, while the civil and military ministers hastened to court. Taizong asked, “To what office should Chen Guangrui, the new principal graduate, be appointed?” Chancellor Wei Zheng memorialized, “I have examined the prefectures and districts under Your Majesty’s rule. There is a vacancy in Jiangzhou; I beg my sovereign to appoint him to that post.” Taizong accordingly appointed him governor of Jiangzhou and ordered him to make ready and depart at once, without missing the prescribed deadline. Guangrui thanked the emperor for his grace and withdrew from court. Returning to the chancellor’s residence, he consulted his wife, bade farewell to his father- and mother-in-law, and set out with her to assume his post in Jiangzhou. They left Chang’an and took to the road.

p.src: It was late spring: gentle winds stirred the green willows, and fine rain speckled the red blossoms. Guangrui stopped at his home, and together with his wife bowed before his mother, Madam Zhang. Madam Zhang said, “Congratulations, my son—and you have even returned with a bride.” Guangrui said, “Through the blessing of Mother’s good fortune, your unworthy son was fortunate enough to place first. By imperial command I was paraded through the streets, and when I passed Chancellor Yin’s residence, the embroidered ball cast to choose a husband struck me. The chancellor then graciously chose your son as his daughter’s husband. The court has appointed your son governor of Jiangzhou. I have now come to fetch you so that we may proceed together to my post.” Madam Zhang was overjoyed and prepared for the journey.

p.src: After several days on the road, they reached the Wanhua Inn, kept by Liu Xiao’er, and lodged there. Madam Zhang suddenly fell ill and said to Guangrui, “I am unwell. Let us remain at the inn for two days while I recover, and then continue.” Guangrui obeyed. Early the next morning, he saw a man outside the inn hawking a golden carp, and Guangrui bought it for one string of cash. He was about to have it cooked for his mother when he saw the carp blinking its eyes. Guangrui said in astonishment, “I have heard that when fish and snakes blink their eyes, they cannot be ordinary creatures.” He therefore asked the fisherman, “Where did you catch this fish?” The fisherman replied, “I caught it in the Hong River, fifteen li from the prefectural city.” Guangrui took the fish to the Hong River and released it. When he returned to the inn, he told his mother what he had done. Madam Zhang said, “Releasing a living creature is a good deed. It pleases me greatly.” Guangrui said, “We have stayed at this inn for three days, and the imperial deadline presses. Your son wishes to depart tomorrow, but I do not know whether Mother has recovered.” Madam Zhang replied, “I am still unwell, and the road is hot at this season. I fear my illness may worsen. Rent a room for me here to stay in for the time being, and leave me some traveling expenses. You and your wife should go on ahead to your post. When the cool autumn weather comes, return and fetch me.” Guangrui consulted his wife, rented a house, and left his mother money for expenses. Then he and his wife bowed farewell and continued on their way.

p.src: The road was arduous. Traveling by day and lodging by night, they reached the Hong River ferry before they knew it. There they saw two boatmen, Liu Hong and Li Biao, pole their boat to the bank to receive them. It must have been Guangrui’s fate from a former life to suffer this calamity, for here he encountered his mortal enemies. Guangrui ordered the household servant to carry their luggage aboard. Just as husband and wife were boarding together, Liu Hong opened his eyes wide and saw that Lady Yin’s face was like the full moon, her eyes like autumn waters, her little mouth like a cherry, and her slender waist like a green willow. Hers was truly a beauty that would make fish sink and geese fall, the moon hide and flowers blush. A wolfish desire suddenly arose in his heart. He plotted with Li Biao, and together they poled the boat to a deserted place. They waited until the dead of night at the third watch, then first killed the household servant and next beat Guangrui to death, pushing both corpses into the water. When the young lady saw them kill her husband, she too tried to throw herself into the river. Liu Hong seized her in his arms and said, “If you submit to me, the matter ends here; if you refuse, I shall cut you in two with one stroke.” The young lady could think of no escape, so she had no choice but to feign consent for the moment and yield to Liu Hong. The villain ferried the boat to the southern bank and left it in Li Biao’s charge. He then put on Guangrui’s official robes and cap, took his credentials, and went with the young lady to Jiangzhou to assume office.

p.src: Now the corpse of the household servant whom Liu Hong had murdered drifted away with the current. Only Chen Guangrui’s corpse sank to the riverbed and remained there without moving. A sea-patrolling yaksha at the mouth of the Hong River saw it and flew like a shooting star to report at the Dragon Palace. The Dragon King was just holding court when the yaksha announced, “Someone has beaten a young scholar to death at the mouth of the Hong River and cast his corpse upon the riverbed.” The Dragon King ordered the corpse brought before him. After examining it closely, he said, “This man is none other than my benefactor who saved me. How has he come to be murdered? As the saying goes, ‘Repay kindness with kindness.’ Today I must save his life and repay the kindness he showed me the other day.” He immediately wrote an official dispatch and sent the yaksha straight to the City God and Earth God of Hongzhou, requesting the scholar’s soul so that his life might be restored. The City God and Earth God summoned a minor ghost and had Chen Guangrui’s soul handed over to the yaksha. The yaksha brought the soul to the Crystal Palace and presented himself before the Dragon King.

p.src: The Dragon King asked, “What is your surname and given name, scholar? Where are you from? Why did you come here, and how were you beaten to death?” Guangrui bowed and replied, “This humble scholar is Chen E, courtesy name Guangrui, a native of Hongnong County in Haizhou. I had the undeserved honor of placing first in the latest imperial examination and was appointed governor of Jiangzhou, so I set out for my post with my wife. When we reached the river and boarded a boat, the boatman Liu Hong, coveting my wife, unexpectedly murdered me and cast away my body. I beg Your Majesty to save me.” Hearing this, the Dragon King said, “So that is what happened. Sir, I was the golden carp you released before. You are my benefactor and saved my life. Now that you are in distress, how could I possibly refuse to save you?” He had Guangrui’s body placed to one side with a Face-Preserving Pearl in its mouth to keep it from decaying, so that one day Guangrui might return to life and avenge himself. Then he said, “For the present, let your true soul serve as a commander in my water palace.” Guangrui kowtowed in gratitude, and the Dragon King gave a banquet in his honor. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now, Miss Yin hated the villain Liu so bitterly that she longed to devour his flesh and sleep upon his hide. Only because she was pregnant and did not yet know whether she bore a son or daughter, she had no choice but to submit to him for the time being. In the blink of an eye, they arrived at Jiangzhou. The clerks, secretaries, gatekeepers, and runners all came to welcome them. The subordinate officials laid a banquet in the public hall to welcome and acquaint themselves with him. Liu Hong said, “Now that I have come here, I must rely entirely upon your generous support.” The subordinate officials replied, “Your Honor possesses the brilliant talents of the foremost graduate. You will naturally cherish the people as your own children, reduce litigation, and administer justice with integrity. All of us under your jurisdiction shall benefit from your governance, so why be so modest?” When the public banquet ended, everyone dispersed.

p.src: Time passed swiftly. One day, Liu Hong went far away on official business. At the yamen, the young lady thought of her mother-in-law and husband and sighed sorrowfully in the flower pavilion. Suddenly she grew weak and weary; pain seized her belly, and she fainted to the ground, whereupon she gave birth to a son without realizing it. A voice beside her ear admonished her: “Mantangjiao, heed my instructions. I am the Lord of the Southern Pole Star. By decree of the Bodhisattva Guanyin, I have specially brought you this child. One day his fame will spread far and wide; he is no ordinary child. If the villain Liu returns, he will surely harm this child, so you must take great care to protect him. Your husband has already been saved by the Dragon King. In time, husband and wife shall meet again, mother and son shall be reunited, and the day will come when your wrongs are redressed and your vengeance taken. Remember my words well. Awake, awake!” With that, the voice departed.

p.src: The young lady awoke remembering every word. She held the child close, but could think of no course to take. Suddenly Liu Hong returned. The moment he saw the child, he wanted to drown him. The young lady said, “It is already late today. Let us wait until tomorrow to cast him into the river.” Fortunately, early the next morning, Liu Hong was suddenly called far away on urgent official business. The young lady thought to herself, “If this child is still here when the villain returns, his life will be over. Better to cast him into the river at once and leave his life or death to fate. If Heaven should take pity and someone rescues and raises him, perhaps we may yet meet again one day.” Fearing, however, that he would be hard to identify, she bit her finger and wrote a letter in blood, setting down in full his parents’ names and the entire story of his origins. She also bit off the child’s left little toe to serve as a mark of identification. Taking an undershirt she wore next to her skin, she wrapped the child in it and, seizing an unobserved moment, carried him out of the yamen. Fortunately, the government office was not far from the river. When the young lady reached the riverbank, she wept bitterly. Just as she was about to abandon the child, she suddenly saw a wooden plank drift up beside the bank. She bowed to Heaven in prayer, placed the child upon the plank, bound him securely with a sash, tied the blood letter to his chest, and pushed him out into the river to go wherever the current might bear him. The young lady returned to the yamen in tears. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now the child drifted downstream upon the wooden plank until at last it stopped at the foot of the Golden Mountain Monastery. The abbot of the Golden Mountain Monastery was a monk named Faming, who had cultivated truth, awakened to the Way, and mastered the wondrous secret of the Unborn. While he was seated in meditation contemplating Chan, he suddenly heard an infant crying. His heart stirred, and he hurried to the riverbank to look. There, on a wooden plank beside the shore, lay a sleeping baby. The abbot hastily rescued him. On finding the blood letter tucked against his breast, he learned the child’s origins. He gave him the childhood name River-Drift and entrusted him to someone to be nursed and raised. He kept the blood letter safely hidden away.

He laid a hand upon his crown, administered the precepts, and Xuanzang devoted himself steadfastly to cultivating the Way.

p.src: One day in late spring, the monks were gathered beneath the shade of the pines, expounding sutras, contemplating Chan, and discussing profound mysteries. A certain wine-and-meat monk happened to be confounded by Xuanzang in debate. The monk flew into a rage and cursed him: “You wretched beast! You do not even know your own name or your parents, yet you come here playing your tricks. What devilry are you up to?” Wounded by these words, Xuanzang went into the monastery, knelt before his master, and said with tears streaming from both eyes, “A person is born between Heaven and Earth, endowed with yin and yang and sustained by the Five Elements; all are begotten by a father and raised by a mother. How could anyone living in this world have no parents?” Again and again he pleaded sorrowfully, begging to know his parents’ names. The abbot said, “If you truly wish to seek your parents, follow me to my quarters.” Xuanzang followed him to the abbot’s quarters. The abbot reached above a crossbeam and took down a small box. Opening it, he removed a blood letter and an undershirt and handed them to Xuanzang. Xuanzang unfolded and read the blood letter. Only then did he learn in full his parents’ names and the story of the wrong done to them.

u.src: One day in late spring, the monks were gathered beneath the shade of the pines, expounding sutras, contemplating Chan, and discussing profound mysteries. A certain wine-and-meat monk happened to be confounded by Xuanzang in debate.
The monk flew into a rage and cursed him: “You wretched beast! You do not even know your own name or your parents, yet you come here playing your tricks. What devilry are you up to?”

Wounded by these words, Xuanzang went into the monastery, knelt before his master, and said with tears streaming from both eyes, “A person is born between Heaven and Earth, endowed with yin and yang and sustained by the Five Elements; all are begotten by a father and raised by a mother. How could anyone living in this world have no parents?”
Again and again he pleaded sorrowfully, begging to know his parents’ names.
The abbot said, “If you truly wish to seek your parents, follow me to my quarters.”
Xuanzang followed him to the abbot’s quarters.
The abbot reached above a crossbeam and took down a small box. Opening it, he removed a blood letter and an undershirt and handed them to Xuanzang.
Xuanzang unfolded and read the blood letter. Only then did he learn in full his parents’ names and the story of the wrong done to them.

p.src: When Xuanzang finished reading, he collapsed weeping to the ground and cried, “If I cannot avenge my parents, how can I call myself a man? For eighteen years I did not know my birth parents, and only today have I learned that my mother still lives. Had you not rescued me from the water and raised me, Master, how could I be alive today? Permit your disciple to go and find his mother. Afterward, I shall bear an incense brazier upon my head and rebuild the temple halls to repay the profound kindness you have shown me.” His master said, “If you wish to seek your mother, take this blood letter and undershirt with you. Pretend merely to be collecting alms and go straight to the private quarters of the Jiangzhou yamen; only there will you be able to meet your mother.”

p.src: Xuanzang obeyed his master’s instructions, took the guise of an alms-seeking monk, and went straight to Jiangzhou. Liu Hong happened to be away on business. It was indeed Heaven’s will that mother and son should meet, and Xuanzang went directly to the gate of the yamen’s private quarters to beg for alms. As it happened, Miss Yin had dreamed during the night that the waning moon had become full again. She thought privately, “I have no news at all of my mother-in-law. My husband was murdered by this villain. My son was cast into the river. If someone rescued and raised him, he would now be eighteen years old. Perhaps Heaven may cause us to meet today; who can say?” While she was pondering this, she suddenly heard someone chanting sutras before the private quarters and repeatedly calling for alms. Taking the opportunity, the young lady went out and asked, “Where have you come from?” Xuanzang replied, “This poor monk is a disciple of the Venerable Faming of the Golden Mountain Monastery.” The young lady said, “Since you are a disciple of the abbot of the Golden Mountain Monastery…” She called him into the yamen and gave Xuanzang a vegetarian meal. She carefully observed his bearing and speech, and found him remarkably like her husband.

p.src: The young lady sent her maidservants away and asked, “Little master, did you enter the monastic life as a child, or only after you had grown up? What are your surname and given name? Do you have parents?” Xuanzang replied, “I neither entered the monastic life as a child nor after I had grown up. My story is one of injustice as vast as heaven and hatred as deep as the sea: my father was murdered, and my mother was seized by the villain. My master, Elder Faming, told me to seek my mother in the Jiangzhou magistrate’s residence.” The young lady asked, “What is your mother’s surname?” Xuanzang said, “My mother’s surname is Yin, and her given name is Wenjiao. My father’s surname is Chen, and his given name is Guangrui. My childhood name is River Float, and my Dharma name is Xuanzang.” The young lady said, “I am Wenjiao. But what proof do you have?” When Xuanzang heard that she was his mother, he fell to his knees and wept bitterly. “Mother, if you do not believe me, I have the letter written in blood and the undershirt as proof.” Wenjiao took them and examined them. They were indeed genuine, and mother and son embraced and wept. Then she cried, “My son, leave quickly.” Xuanzang said, “For eighteen years I did not know my own parents, and only today have I seen my mother. How can you ask your son to tear himself away?” The young lady said, “My son, you must get away at once. If that villain Liu returns, he will surely kill you. Tomorrow I shall pretend to be ill and say that years ago I vowed to donate a hundred pairs of monks’ shoes, so I must come to your monastery to fulfill the vow. Then I shall have something to tell you.” Xuanzang obeyed and bowed farewell.

p.src: Now after seeing her son, the young lady’s heart was filled with both sorrow and joy. One day she suddenly feigned illness, refused all food and drink, and lay in bed. When Liu Hong returned to the magistrate’s residence, he asked what was wrong. The young lady said, “When I was young, I once made a vow to donate a hundred pairs of monks’ shoes. Five days ago I dreamed of a monk holding a sharp blade who demanded the shoes from me, and ever since then I have felt unwell.” Liu Hong said, “Why did you not tell me sooner about such a trifling matter?” He immediately took his seat in the hall and ordered the two subordinate officers, Wang and Li, to require every household in Jiangzhou to furnish one pair of monks’ shoes, all to be delivered within five days. The people all supplied their assigned pairs and completed the delivery. The young lady said to Liu Hong, “Now that the monks’ shoes are finished, what monastery is there here where I may fulfill my vow?” Liu Hong said, “Here in Jiangzhou there are the Golden Mountain Monastery and the Scorched Mountain Monastery. Go to whichever one you please.” The young lady said, “I have long heard that the Golden Mountain Monastery is a splendid temple, so I shall go there.” Liu Hong at once ordered the two officers, Wang and Li, to prepare a boat. The young lady took her trusted attendants aboard with her. The boatman pushed off, and they headed for the Golden Mountain Monastery.

p.src: Xuanzang returned weeping to the monastery. After informing his master, he immediately bowed farewell and set out directly for Hongzhou. Arriving at the Ten Thousand Flowers Inn, he asked the proprietor, Liu Xiao’er, “Years ago, a traveler named Chen from Jiangzhou left his mother at your inn. How is she now?” Liu Xiao’er said, “She did once stay at my inn. Later she lost her sight and for three or four years paid me no rent. Now she lives in a ruined tile kiln by the South Gate and survives by begging in the streets each day. That traveler has been gone a long time, and to this day there has been no word of him. I do not know why.” After hearing this, Xuanzang at once asked his way to the ruined tile kiln by the South Gate and found his grandmother. The old woman said, “Your voice sounds just like that of my son, Chen Guangrui.” Xuanzang said, “I am not Chen Guangrui. I am his son. Lady Wenjiao is my mother.” The old woman asked, “Why have your father and mother not come?” Xuanzang said, “My father was killed by a bandit, and my mother was seized by the bandit and forced to become his wife.” The old woman asked, “How did you know to come and seek me?” Xuanzang said, “My mother sent me to find you. I have a letter from her here, as well as an incense ring.” The old woman took the letter and the incense ring and wailed aloud, “My son came here in pursuit of rank and distinction. I thought only that he had forgotten honor and gratitude, never knowing that he had been murdered. Yet happily, Heaven has shown compassion and has not cut off my son’s line; today his own son has come to find me.” Xuanzang asked, “Grandmother, how did you lose the sight of both eyes?” The old woman said, “I missed your father and watched anxiously for him day after day, but he never came. I wept until both my eyes went blind.”

p.src: Xuanzang knelt and prayed to Heaven, saying, “I, Xuanzang, am now eighteen years old, yet I have been unable to avenge my parents. Today, at my mother’s command, I have come to seek my grandmother. If Heaven will look with compassion upon this disciple’s sincerity, may my grandmother’s eyes be restored to sight.” When he had finished praying, he used the tip of his tongue to lick his grandmother’s eyes. In a moment her eyes opened, and her sight was restored as before. The old woman peered at the young monk and said, “You truly are my grandson. You look exactly like my son Guangrui.” The old woman was both joyful and sorrowful. Xuanzang led his grandmother out through the kiln entrance and returned with her to Liu Xiao’er’s inn. He used some money to rent a room where his grandmother could live. He also gave her traveling money and said, “I am leaving now, but I shall return in a little over a month.”

p.src: He immediately took leave of his grandmother and went straight to the capital. He found Chancellor Yin's residence on the eastern street of the imperial city and told the gatekeeper, “This humble monk is a relative who has come to visit His Excellency.” The gatekeeper reported this to the chancellor, who said, “I have no monks among my kin.” His wife said, “Last night I dreamed that our daughter Mantangjiao came home. Could our son-in-law have sent us a letter?” The chancellor then ordered that the young monk be shown into the hall. When the young monk saw the chancellor and his wife, he fell to the floor before them, weeping, then took a letter from inside his robe and handed it to the chancellor. The chancellor opened it and read it from beginning to end, then burst into loud sobs. His wife asked, “My lord, what has happened?” The chancellor said, “This monk is your grandson and mine. Our son-in-law Chen Guangrui was murdered by a bandit, and Mantangjiao was forcibly taken by that villain as his wife.” On hearing this, his wife also wept inconsolably. The chancellor said, “Do not grieve, my lady. Tomorrow I shall report this to His Majesty and personally lead an army to avenge our son-in-law.”

p.src: The next day the chancellor went to court and memorialized the Tang emperor: “My son-in-law, Chen Guangrui, the top graduate in the imperial examination, was traveling with his household to take up his post in Jiangzhou when the boatman Liu Hong murdered him and seized my daughter as his wife. That villain has impersonated my son-in-law and held office for many years. This is an extraordinary outrage. I beg Your Majesty to dispatch troops at once and destroy these criminals.” The Tang emperor was enraged by the memorial. He immediately mobilized sixty thousand imperial guards and appointed Chancellor Yin to command them. The chancellor received the decree and left the court. He went straight to the drill ground, mustered the troops, and set out for Jiangzhou. Traveling by day and lodging by night, setting out when the stars faded and the birds took flight, they reached Jiangzhou before they knew it, and Chancellor Yin's entire army made camp on the northern bank. That very night he sent an urgent summons to the assistant prefect and the judicial official of Jiangzhou. When the two arrived, the chancellor explained the matter and ordered them to bring troops to his aid, whereupon they all crossed the river together. Before dawn, they surrounded Liu Hong's yamen. Liu Hong was still dreaming when a cannon boomed and gongs and drums sounded together. The soldiers stormed his private quarters, and before he could react he was seized. The chancellor issued a military order to bind Liu Hong and all his accomplices and take them to the execution ground, while the army was sent to make camp outside the city.

p.src: The chancellor went straight into the main hall of the yamen, seated himself, and asked that his daughter come out to meet him. She was about to come out, but was too ashamed to face her father and tried to hang herself. When Xuanzang heard of this, he rushed to save his mother. Kneeling before her, he said, “Your son has come here with Grandfather at the head of an army to avenge Father. Now that the villain has been captured, Mother, why do you seek death instead? If you die, Mother, how could your son go on living?” The chancellor also entered the yamen and tried to console her. She said, “I have heard it said that a woman must remain faithful to one husband until her death. My beloved husband was slain by a villain; how could I shamelessly submit to that villain? Only because I was carrying his posthumous child did I endure the shame and cling to life. Now, happily, my son is grown, and I have seen my aged father bring an army to avenge us. How can I, as your daughter, have the face to meet you? Only by dying can I repay my husband.” The chancellor said, “My child, you did not change your fidelity with the rise and fall of fortune. Everything happened because you had no choice. What cause have you for shame?” Father and daughter embraced and wept, while Xuanzang too sobbed without cease. Wiping away his tears, the chancellor said, “You two must set aside your grief for now. Now that I have captured our mortal enemy, I must go and see that he is dealt with.” He rose at once and went to the execution ground. Just then, the assistant prefect of Jiangzhou also sent scouts who captured the river bandit Li Biao and brought him in under guard. The chancellor was delighted. He ordered the military guards to bring Liu Hong and Li Biao forward and give each of them one hundred heavy strokes. Their depositions were taken, and they confessed how they had conspired years before to murder Chen Guangrui. Li Biao was first nailed to the wooden donkey, wheeled to the marketplace, cut to pieces by a thousand slashes, and beheaded, his head displayed as a warning to all. Liu Hong was taken to the Hong River ferry, the place where he had murdered Chen Guangrui years before. The chancellor, his daughter, and Xuanzang all went in person to the riverbank. They offered sacrifices beneath the open sky, cut the living Liu Hong's heart and liver from his body as an offering to Guangrui, and burned a sacrificial address.

p.src: As the three wept toward the river, their lamentations soon stirred the underwater palace, and a sea-patrolling yaksha presented the sacrificial address to the Dragon King. After reading it, the Dragon King sent Marshal Turtle to bring Guangrui before him and said, “Congratulations, sir, congratulations! Your wife, your son, and your father-in-law are all now on the riverbank making offerings to you. I shall now send you back to return to life. I also present you with one wish-fulfilling pearl, two rolling-plate pearls, ten bolts of twisted silk, and a jade belt set with bright pearls. This very day you may be reunited with your wife and son.” Guangrui bowed repeatedly in thanks. The Dragon King then ordered the yaksha to carry Guangrui's body out to the river mouth and restore his soul to it. The yaksha received the order and departed.

Your wife, your son, and your father-in-law are all now on the riverbank making offerings to you.
I shall now send you back to return to life.
I also present you with one wish-fulfilling pearl, two rolling-plate pearls, ten bolts of twisted silk, and a jade belt set with bright pearls.

p.src: Now after Lady Yin had wept and made offerings for her husband, she again tried to throw herself into the river and die, making Xuanzang desperately seize and hold her back. Amid the confusion, they suddenly saw a corpse floating across the water toward the riverbank. She hurried forward to examine it and recognized her husband's body, whereupon she wailed more bitterly than ever. Everyone gathered to look. Before their eyes, Guangrui unclenched his fists and stretched his legs; his body gradually began to move, and suddenly he raised himself and sat up. Everyone was overwhelmed with astonishment. Guangrui opened his eyes and at once saw Lady Yin, his father-in-law Chancellor Yin, and the young monk all beside him, weeping. Guangrui asked, “Why are you all here?” His wife said, “After the villain murdered you, I gave birth to this son. Fortunately, the elder of Gold Mountain Monastery raised him to adulthood. When he found me and we were reunited, I told him to seek out his grandfather. When Father learned what had happened, he reported it to the court and led an army here. He captured the villains and just now cut the heart and liver from one of them alive, offering them beneath the open sky to you, my husband. But how is it that you have returned to life?” Guangrui said, “It is all because, years ago at the Myriad Flowers Inn, you and I bought and released that golden carp. Who would have known that the carp was the Dragon King of this place? Later, when the traitorous villains pushed me into the water, it was entirely thanks to him that I was saved. Just now he restored me to life and gave me treasures, all of which I have upon me. I never imagined that you had borne me this son, or that Father-in-law would avenge me. Truly, bitterness is ended and sweetness has come. There could be no greater joy.”

p.src: When the officials heard what had happened, they all came to offer their congratulations. The chancellor ordered a banquet prepared to thank the officials under his command. That very day the army began its return journey. When they reached the Myriad Flowers Inn, the chancellor ordered the army to make camp. Guangrui and Xuanzang then went together to the Liu Family Inn to look for his mother. That night the old woman had dreamed of a withered tree bursting into blossom, while magpies chattered incessantly behind the house. She thought, “Could my grandson be coming?” Before she had finished speaking, Guangrui and his son appeared together outside the inn door. The young monk pointed and said, “Is that not my grandmother?” When Guangrui saw his aged mother, he hurriedly fell to his knees before her. Mother and son embraced and wept bitterly, and he told her everything that had happened. They settled the inn bill with the waiter, set out, and returned to the capital. After entering the chancellor's residence, Guangrui, his wife, his mother, and Xuanzang all went to pay their respects to the chancellor's wife. The chancellor's wife was overjoyed and ordered the servants to prepare a grand celebratory feast. The chancellor said, “Today's feast may fittingly be called the Reunion Banquet.” The whole family was truly filled with joy.

p.src: At the morning court the next day, the Tang emperor ascended the throne. Chancellor Yin stepped forward from the ranks and reported the whole affair in full detail, also recommending Guangrui as a man whose talents merited high office. The Tang emperor approved his petition and at once appointed Chen E to the office of academician, charging him to attend the court and assist in governing the realm. Xuanzang had resolved to devote himself to meditation, so he was sent to Hongfu Monastery to pursue his religious practice. Later, in the end, Miss Yin calmly took her own life. Xuanzang himself went to Jinshan Monastery to repay the kindness of Elder Faming.
